title: Convergent lifting of split-node coordinates
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ and $(B,\mathfrak n)$ be commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for their maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $\alpha:A\to B$ be a local homomorphism, meaning $\alpha(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Set $k=A/\mathfrak m$ and fix a $k$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:k[[x,y]]/(xy)\xrightarrow{\sim}B/\mathfrak mB$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], where $\mathfrak mB$ is the ideal generated by $\alpha(\mathfrak m)$. Write $\bar u=\theta(x)$ and $\bar v=\theta(y)$. For every choice of lifts $u_1,v_1\in B$ of $\bar u,\bar v$, there exist sequences $(u_r,v_r,h_r)_{r\ge1}$ starting with these $u_1,v_1$ and $h_1=0$, with $u_r,v_r\in\mathfrak n$ lifting $\bar u,\bar v$ and $h_r\in\mathfrak m$, such that $u_rv_r-\alpha(h_r)\in\mathfrak m^rB$, $u_{r+1}-u_r,v_{r+1}-v_r\in\mathfrak m^rB$, and $h_{r+1}-h_r\in\mathfrak m^r$. These sequences converge in the respective maximal-ideal-adic topologies to $u,v\in\mathfrak n$ and $h\in\mathfrak m$, with $u,v$ still lifting $\bar u,\bar v$ and $uv=\alpha(h)$. Here convergence means eventual agreement modulo every fixed power of the respective maximal ideal; no $\mathfrak mB$-adic completeness hypothesis on $B$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family, second paragraph and the induction and limits in the third paragraph.

proof.text: Put $I=\mathfrak mB\subseteq\mathfrak n$. In $k[[x,y]]/(xy)$ neither $x$ nor $y$ is a unit, since the constant coefficient of any multiple of either is zero. Hence no lift $u_1,v_1$ is a unit in $B$, so both lie in its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. Their product reduces to $xy=0$, so $u_1v_1\in I$; with $h_1=0$ this is the induction base.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family, second paragraph and induction/limits in the third paragraph.

proof.text: For any lifts $u,v$ and any $b\in B$, represent $\theta^{-1}(b\bmod I)$ by $F\in k[[x,y]]$. Coefficientwise partition the nonconstant monomials into those divisible by $x$ and those with $x$-exponent zero and positive $y$-exponent. This gives $F=c+xP+yQ$ with $c\in k$ and $P,Q\in k[[x,y]]$. Lift $c$ to $a\in A$ and the images $\theta(P),\theta(Q)$ to $p,q\in B$. Then $b=\alpha(a)+up+vq+\epsilon$ with $\epsilon\in I$. This is a coefficientwise identity, not an assertion about arbitrary maps being determined by the variables.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family, second paragraph and induction/limits in the third paragraph.

proof.text: Suppose $r\ge1$, $h_r\in\mathfrak m$, and $\delta=u_rv_r-\alpha(h_r)\in\mathfrak m^rB$. By the definition of extended ideal, write a finite sum $\delta=\sum_i\alpha(f_i)b_i$ with $f_i\in\mathfrak m^r$. Step 2 gives $b_i=\alpha(a_i)+u_rp_i+v_rq_i+\epsilon_i$, $\epsilon_i\in I$. Set $P_r=\sum_i\alpha(f_i)p_i$, $Q_r=\sum_i\alpha(f_i)q_i$, and $d_r=\sum_i f_i a_i\in\mathfrak m^r$. Define $u_{r+1}=u_r-Q_r$, $v_{r+1}=v_r-P_r$, $h_{r+1}=h_r+d_r$. Multiplication gives $u_{r+1}v_{r+1}-\alpha(h_{r+1})=\sum_i\alpha(f_i)\epsilon_i+Q_rP_r\in\mathfrak m^{r+1}B$, because $2r\ge r+1$. The differences have the required orders; $h_{r+1}\in\mathfrak m$ and $u_{r+1},v_{r+1}$ retain their reductions and remain in $\mathfrak n$. Recursively choose such finite expressions to obtain the sequences for all $r\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family, second paragraph and induction/limits in the third paragraph.

proof.text: For $s>r$, telescoping the differences gives $u_s-u_r,v_s-v_r\in\mathfrak m^rB\subseteq\mathfrak n^r$ and $h_s-h_r\in\mathfrak m^r$. Thus for every $N\ge1$ the classes of these sequences modulo $\mathfrak n^N,\mathfrak n^N,\mathfrak m^N$ stabilize for $r\ge N$. The stabilized classes are compatible under all quotient projections. Apply the inverse-limit definition of completeness to obtain $u,v\in B$ and $h\in A$ representing them. In particular $u-u_r,v-v_r\in\mathfrak n^N$ and $h-h_r\in\mathfrak m^N$ for $r\ge N$, which is exactly the stated convergence. Taking $N=1$ gives $u,v\in\mathfrak n$ and $h\in\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family, second paragraph and induction/limits in the third paragraph.

proof.text: Apply the complete-local-quotient theorem to $R=B$ and the proper ideal $I=\mathfrak mB\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Its hypotheses are the assumed Noetherianity, locality and $\mathfrak n$-adic completeness. It gives $\bar B=B/I$ complete for its maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak n}=\mathfrak n/I$, hence $\bigcap_N\bar{\mathfrak n}^N=0$ by the completeness definition. For every $N$ choose $r\ge N$: since $u_r-u_1\in I$ and $u-u_r\in\mathfrak n^N$, the class of $u-u_1$ belongs to $\bar{\mathfrak n}^N$. It is therefore zero; the same argument for $v-v_1$ shows that $u,v$ still lift $\bar u,\bar v$. This spells out the needed closedness of $I$ without assuming $I$-adic completeness of $B$.

source.place: Tag 0325, lemma-quotient-complete-local, first sentence; applied to the limit argument of Tag 0CBX.

proof.text: Fix $N\ge1$ and choose $r\ge N$. Locality of $\alpha$ gives $\alpha(\mathfrak m^N)\subseteq\mathfrak n^N$. We have $uv-u_rv_r=(u-u_r)v+u_r(v-v_r)\in\mathfrak n^N$, $\alpha(h-h_r)\in\mathfrak n^N$, and $u_rv_r-\alpha(h_r)\in\mathfrak m^rB\subseteq\mathfrak n^N$. Adding these congruences gives $uv-\alpha(h)\in\mathfrak n^N$ for every $N$. The separatedness included in $\mathfrak n$-adic completeness forces $uv=\alpha(h)$, finishing all the assertions.
